full_judgment:
12. Here, there is no dispute that the property in question had in fact vested, rightly or wrongly, in the Government on 28-02-1972 by operation of PO No. 16 of 1972.There is also no dispute that the same has subsequently been divested through the aforesaid sale by Government in exercise of power under Articles-4 and 5(2) (e) & (i) of PO No. 16 of 1972.Now, under such circumstances, can there be any presumption, for any practical purpose, under sub-section (2) of section 5 of the Ordinance that the said property again vested in the Government on 28-2-1972 under PO No. 16 of 1972? In other words, can the same property vest twice? Or can there be double-presumptions, or can a matter already closed under the parent law be reopened subsequently under the supplemental law? The answer to all these .questions is 'No'. We find support of our this view in Sarwari Begum vs Bangladesh, 45 DLR 571 (at para 16). In this case, a' division bench of this Court also held (at para 17.& 18) that in such situation the petitioner can directly come to the High Court Division under Article 102(1) for enforcement of his/her fundamental' right to property guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution. 

 13. There is no such provision of double vesting or double-presumption either in PO No. 16 of 1972 or in Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. Thus, if a property is included in the list published under section 5(i)(a) of the said Ordinance even after the said property is admittedly divested, that inclusion is nothing but either a result of mistake on the face of it or is a product of non-application of mind by the officials vested with the responsibility or prepare the list, In both' situations, the inclusion is an act without jurisdiction and, as such, the said property should be deemed to have never included in the said list on the principle that an act without jurisdiction is an act never existed in the eye of law (void abinitio). Therefore, since the inclusion of the said property in the 'Ka' list is a non-existent act, we are of the view that, it does not carry with it any presumption or legal consequences as provided by sections 5(2), 6 and 7 of the said Ordinance as submitted by Mr Mahbubey Alam. Accordingly, the decisions of our apex court, as cited by Mr Alam on the point of presumption and legal consequences of inclusion of a building in the 'Ka' list, are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 14. In the present case, since the said property has been included apparently as a result of either mistake or non-application of mind, the question of discharging any onus by the petitioner does not arise. Here the Government itself rebutted the presumption by its acts. Here the petitioner has stepped into the shoes of the said Austrian Lady and, as such, there is no onus on him to prove that the said property is not an abandoned property - because of the fact that the said property was divested by the Government itself in accordance with law and the inclusion of the same in the 'Ka' list in an act without jurisdiction. Thus, since the inclusion in the said list never existed in the eye of law, we are also dis-inclined to agree with the submissions of Mr Alam to the effect that the suit and the decree in question were barred by section 6 of the said Ordinance or that the petitioner should first go to the Court of Settlement under section 7 - even long after expiry of limitation period of 180 days. We are of the view that the unique facts in the present case deserve different approach, if not unique approach.
